problem:
Let $v=[\begin{aligned}x \\ 2x \\ 4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}3x \\ -3 \\ x \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
If $v\cdot w=-2$ and $x>0$, find the value of $x.$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Value of an Unknown Quantity in an Expression Involving the Dot Product
examples.problem: Let be $[\begin{aligned}10 \\ x \\ 0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]$ and $[\begin{aligned}x \\ x \\ 8 \\ 5\end{aligned}]$ If $\mathbf{a}\cdot \mathbf{b}=0,$ find the value of $x.$
examples.worked_solution:
Starting from the equation $\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}=0,$ we compute the dot product in terms of $x$ and then solve for $x$ in the resulting equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ 10\cdot x+x\cdot x+0\cdot 8+5\cdot 5 & =0 \\ 10x+{x}^{2}+25 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+10x+25 & =0 \\ (x+5)^{2} & =0 \\ x & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $x=-5.$

To compute the dot product, we add up the products of corresponding components:

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & ={p}_{1}\cdot {q}_{1}+{p}_{2}\cdot {q}_{2}+{p}_{3}\cdot {q}_{3}+{p}_{4}\cdot {q}_{4}+{p}_{5}\cdot {q}_{5} \\  & =(-5)\cdot 2+4\cdot (-1)+(-1)\cdot 4+3\cdot (-3)+(-2)\cdot 5 \\  & =-10-4-4-9-10 \\  & =-37\end{aligned}
$$
